auxiliary_material: The authors discussed the broader context of ubiquitin pathway enzymes in immune regulation, noting that NEDD8 inhibition can suppress immune suppressive cells (MDSCs, TAMs) and that CSN5 depletion enhances anti-CTLA4 drug efficacy. They mentioned a phase I trial combining the SAE inhibitor TAK-981 with pembrolizumab, indicating clinical interest in combining ubiquitin pathway targeting with immune checkpoint inhibitors, though this specific trial does not focus on UBA6.
outline_action: Search for primary studies or specific immunotherapy cohorts (e.g., IMvigor210, Hellmann et al. datasets) that have performed transcriptomic or proteomic analysis including UBA6. Investigate whether UBA6 expression correlates with PD-L1 status, tumor mutational burden, or T-cell infiltration in public databases, as these might serve as proxies for ICI efficacy if direct response data is unavailable. Verify if any ongoing trials targeting E1 enzymes stratify patients by UBA6 expression.
remaining_gap: The supplied material does not contain data linking UBA6 expression specifically to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy in human cohorts. The survival data provided is for overall survival in untreated or mixed populations (TCGA), not ICI response rates or progression-free survival in ICI-treated cohorts. No large-scale validation data (beyond n=22) connecting UBA6 levels to ICI outcomes is presented in this text.
useful_material: This study performed multiomics analyses using TCGA and CPTAC databases to profile UBA6 expression across tumor types. It reported that UBA6 mRNA levels were elevated in over 13 tumor types compared to normal tissues, and protein overexpression was observed in colon cancer and head and neck squamous cancer. Kaplan–Meier analysis indicated that high tumoral UBA6 levels were associated with worse overall survival in lung adenocarcinoma, kidney chromophobe, and clear cell renal cell carcinoma. The review also summarized that UBA6 knockdown suppressed growth in only 10.9% of analyzed cancer cell lines (n=582) in a CRISPR/Cas9 screening.
